scenarios.name: Non-numeric purchase price causes unhandled 500
scenarios.description: nullableString transform passes 'abc' through to numeric(10,4) column causing an unhandled Postgres type error
actions: Create a product payload with purchasePrice set to 'abc'
Submit via POST /api/inventory/products
Verify response status and body
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 with a field-level validation error on purchasePrice
scenarios.actualResult: Unhandled 500 from Postgres numeric type cast failure

scenarios.name: Non-numeric selling price causes unhandled 500
scenarios.description: nullableString transform passes 'abc' through to numeric(10,2) selling price column causing an unhandled Postgres type error
actions: Create a product payload with sellingPrice set to 'abc'
Submit via POST /api/inventory/products
Verify response status and body
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 with a field-level validation error on sellingPrice
scenarios.actualResult: Unhandled 500 from Postgres numeric type cast failure

scenarios.name: Non-numeric safety stock causes unhandled 500
scenarios.description: safetyStock field has no .refine() numeric check so 'abc' passes Zod and hits Postgres as a raw string
actions: Create a product payload with safetyStock set to 'abc'
Submit via POST /api/inventory/products
Verify response status and body
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 with a field-level validation error on safetyStock
scenarios.actualResult: Unhandled 500 from Postgres numeric type cast failure

scenarios.name: Negative safety stock stored in DB
scenarios.description: safetyStock has no non-negative refinement unlike stock, so '-10' passes validation and is stored in the database
actions: Create a product payload with safetyStock set to '-10'
Submit via POST /api/inventory/products
Verify response status
Query DB to confirm value was stored
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 rejecting negative safety stock values
scenarios.actualResult: 201 created with negative safety stock stored in the database

scenarios.name: Non-numeric BOM quantity causes unhandled 500
scenarios.description: nullableString transform on BOM quantity passes 'abc' to numeric column causing unhandled Postgres error
actions: Create a product payload with a BOM row where quantity is 'abc' and bomMode is 'quantity'
Submit via POST /api/inventory/products
Verify response status and body
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 with a field-level validation error on the BOM row quantity
scenarios.actualResult: Unhandled 500 from Postgres numeric type cast failure

scenarios.name: Non-numeric BOM percentage causes unhandled 500
scenarios.description: nullableString transform on BOM percentage passes 'abc' to numeric(5,2) column causing unhandled Postgres error
actions: Create a product payload with a BOM row where percentage is 'abc' and bomMode is 'percentage'
Submit via POST /api/inventory/products
Verify response status and body
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 with a field-level validation error on the BOM row percentage
scenarios.actualResult: Unhandled 500 from Postgres numeric type cast failure

scenarios.name: Switching BOM mode to percentage leaves stale quantity in form state
scenarios.description: When switching bomMode from quantity to percentage, the old quantity value remains in form state and both fields are submitted to the API
actions: Render product form with BOM mode set to quantity
Enter '10' in a BOM row quantity field
Switch bomMode to percentage
Enter '50' in the BOM row percentage field
Submit form
Inspect submitted payload for stale quantity value
scenarios.expectedResult: Only percentage is submitted; quantity is cleared to null
scenarios.actualResult: Both quantity '10' and percentage '50' are submitted, causing ambiguous data

scenarios.name: Switching BOM mode to quantity leaves stale percentage in form state
scenarios.description: When switching bomMode from percentage to quantity, the old percentage value remains in form state and both fields are submitted to the API
actions: Render product form with BOM mode set to percentage
Enter '50' in a BOM row percentage field
Switch bomMode to quantity
Enter '10' in the BOM row quantity field
Submit form
Inspect submitted payload for stale percentage value
scenarios.expectedResult: Only quantity is submitted; percentage is cleared to null
scenarios.actualResult: Both percentage '50' and quantity '10' are submitted, causing ambiguous data

scenarios.name: Whitespace-only name passes validation
scenarios.description: z.string().min(1) has no .trim() so a name of '   ' (spaces only) passes validation and creates an item with a blank display name
actions: Parse the item schema with name set to '   ' (three spaces)
Verify parse result
scenarios.expectedResult: Zod rejects the whitespace-only name with a validation error
scenarios.actualResult: Zod accepts '   ' because .min(1) counts whitespace characters, blank name stored in DB

scenarios.name: Name exceeding varchar(255) causes unhandled 500
scenarios.description: Zod schema has no .max(255) on name field so a 300-character name passes validation and causes a Postgres varchar overflow error
actions: Create a product payload with name set to a 300-character string
Submit via POST /api/inventory/products
Verify response status and body
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 with a validation error about name length
scenarios.actualResult: Unhandled 500 from Postgres varchar(255) overflow

scenarios.name: SKU exceeding varchar(50) causes unhandled 500
scenarios.description: Zod schema has no .max(50) on SKU field so a 60-character SKU passes validation and causes a Postgres varchar overflow error
actions: Create a product payload with sku set to a 60-character string
Submit via POST /api/inventory/products
Verify response status and body
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 with a validation error about SKU length
scenarios.actualResult: Unhandled 500 from Postgres varchar(50) overflow

scenarios.name: Category exceeding varchar(100) causes unhandled 500
scenarios.description: Zod schema has no .max(100) on category field so a 120-character category passes validation and causes a Postgres varchar overflow error
actions: Create a product payload with category set to a 120-character string
Submit via POST /api/inventory/products
Verify response status and body
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 with a validation error about category length
scenarios.actualResult: Unhandled 500 from Postgres varchar(100) overflow

scenarios.name: Scientific notation stock value rejected by Postgres
scenarios.description: '1e5' passes the Zod Number() refinement check but the raw string is inserted into Postgres which rejects scientific notation for numeric columns
actions: Create a product payload with stock set to '1e5'
Submit via POST /api/inventory/products
Verify response status and body
scenarios.expectedResult: Zod normalizes '1e5' to '100000' or rejects it with a clear error
scenarios.actualResult: Unhandled 500 because Postgres rejects scientific notation in numeric column

scenarios.name: Duplicate SKU returns generic 500 instead of field error
scenarios.description: Database unique constraint violation on (org, sku) returns a generic 500 instead of a user-friendly field-level error
actions: Create a product with sku 'TEST-001'
Create a second product with sku 'TEST-001' in the same org
Verify response status and body of second request
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 with { errors: { sku: 'SKU already exists' } }
scenarios.actualResult: Unhandled 500 from Postgres unique constraint violation

scenarios.name: BOM percentage exceeding numeric(5,2) causes unhandled 500
scenarios.description: '1000' exceeds numeric(5,2) max of 999.99 and causes unhandled Postgres overflow error
actions: Create a product payload with a BOM row where percentage is '1000' and bomMode is 'percentage'
Submit via POST /api/inventory/products
Verify response status and body
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 with validation error that percentage must be between 0 and 100
scenarios.actualResult: Unhandled 500 from Postgres numeric(5,2) overflow

scenarios.name: Purchase price exceeding numeric(10,4) causes unhandled 500
scenarios.description: '9999999999' exceeds numeric(10,4) column capacity and causes unhandled Postgres overflow error
actions: Create a product payload with purchasePrice set to '9999999999'
Submit via POST /api/inventory/products
Verify response status and body
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 with validation error about price exceeding maximum
scenarios.actualResult: Unhandled 500 from Postgres numeric(10,4) overflow

scenarios.name: Rapid double-click submits form twice
scenarios.description: The isPending guard in the submit handler closure can be stale on rapid clicks, allowing two submissions before the first mutation marks isPending as true
actions: Render product form with valid data
Trigger onSubmit twice in rapid succession (within 10ms)
Count how many API calls were made
scenarios.expectedResult: Only one API call is made; second click is ignored
scenarios.actualResult: Two API calls are made because isPending is false for both clicks in the same event loop tick

scenarios.name: Stale garbage value in hidden field bypasses superRefine and reaches DB
scenarios.description: Typing 'abc' in quantity field then switching bomMode to percentage leaves the garbage value in form state; superRefine only validates the active mode's field, so 'abc' is submitted to the DB
actions: Render product form with bomMode set to quantity
Enter 'abc' in a BOM row quantity field
Switch bomMode to percentage
Enter '50' in the BOM row percentage field
Submit form
Verify that 'abc' quantity value is not sent to API
scenarios.expectedResult: Quantity field is cleared to null when bomMode switches to percentage
scenarios.actualResult: Stale 'abc' value persists in form state and is submitted alongside percentage, causing a 500 at DB layer

scenarios.name: Corrupted BOM row with both qty and pct re-saves both on every edit
scenarios.description: Once a BOM row has both quantity and percentage stored in the DB (from stale form state), the edit form loads both values and re-saves both on every subsequent edit, making the corruption permanent
actions: Seed a BOM row in DB with both quantity='10' and percentage='50'
Load the product edit form
Change only the product name
Submit the form
Verify DB still has both quantity and percentage on the BOM row
scenarios.expectedResult: Edit form detects the conflict and clears the inactive field, or API rejects ambiguous rows
scenarios.actualResult: Both values are loaded into form state and re-saved, perpetuating the corruption indefinitely

scenarios.name: Concurrent stock edits compute delta against stale value
scenarios.description: Two users editing stock simultaneously both compute delta against the same original value, so the second write produces an incorrect stock level
actions: Set product stock to 100 in DB
User A loads edit form (sees stock=100), changes to 110
User B loads edit form (sees stock=100), changes to 120
User A submits (stock becomes 110)
User B submits (stock becomes 120 instead of 130)
Verify final stock value
scenarios.expectedResult: Final stock is 130 (100 + 10 from A + 20 from B) via optimistic locking or delta-based updates
scenarios.actualResult: Final stock is 120 because User B's write overwrites User A's change with an absolute value

scenarios.name: Negative purchase price stored in DB
scenarios.description: No non-negative refinement on purchasePrice allows '-10.50' to pass Zod validation and be stored, corrupting cost calculations
actions: Create a product payload with purchasePrice set to '-10.50'
Submit via POST /api/inventory/products
Verify the value is stored in DB
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 rejecting negative purchase price
scenarios.actualResult: 201 created with negative purchase price stored in the database

scenarios.name: Negative selling price stored in DB
scenarios.description: No non-negative refinement on sellingPrice allows '-5.00' to pass Zod validation and be stored, corrupting revenue calculations
actions: Create a product payload with sellingPrice set to '-5.00'
Submit via POST /api/inventory/products
Verify the value is stored in DB
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 rejecting negative selling price
scenarios.actualResult: 201 created with negative selling price stored in the database

scenarios.name: Negative BOM quantity stored in DB
scenarios.description: No non-negative check on BOM row quantity allows '-5' to pass validation and be stored, producing nonsensical BOM entries
actions: Create a product payload with a BOM row where quantity is '-5' and bomMode is 'quantity'
Submit via POST /api/inventory/products
Verify the value is stored in DB
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 rejecting negative BOM quantity
scenarios.actualResult: 201 created with negative BOM quantity stored in the database

scenarios.name: BOM percentage total warning is cosmetic only
scenarios.description: The PercentageTotal component shows a warning when percentages don't sum to 100% but the form still submits, allowing incomplete or over-allocated BOMs
actions: Create a product with bomMode 'percentage'
Add BOM rows totaling 90%
Submit the form
Verify the form submits successfully
scenarios.expectedResult: Form is blocked from submitting when percentage total does not equal 100%
scenarios.actualResult: Form submits successfully with 90% total; warning is purely cosmetic

scenarios.name: Selling price silently rounds due to scale mismatch
scenarios.description: sellingPrice uses numeric(10,2) while purchasePrice uses numeric(10,4), so a selling price of '10.1234' silently rounds to '10.12' losing precision
actions: Create a product payload with sellingPrice set to '10.1299'
Submit via POST /api/inventory/products
Query DB for the stored sellingPrice value
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 validation error if more than 2 decimal places, or clear documentation of rounding behavior
scenarios.actualResult: Value silently rounded to '10.13' with no user feedback

scenarios.name: Unit validation error persists after creating a new unit
scenarios.description: After creating a new unit via the inline dialog, setValue is called without shouldValidate:true so the previous 'unit required' error stays visible
actions: Render product form
Submit form without selecting a unit to trigger validation error
Open the create-unit dialog and create a new unit
Verify the new unit is selected
Check whether the unit validation error is still displayed
scenarios.expectedResult: Validation error clears when the new unit is set
scenarios.actualResult: Validation error persists because setValue does not trigger revalidation

scenarios.name: SuperRefine errors shift to wrong BOM row after removal
scenarios.description: When a BOM row is removed via useFieldArray, superRefine validation errors reference stale indices causing errors to appear on the wrong row
actions: Render product form with 3 BOM rows
Trigger a superRefine error on row index 1 (e.g., duplicate component)
Remove row index 0
Verify which row now displays the error
scenarios.expectedResult: Error stays associated with the correct row (now at index 0)
scenarios.actualResult: Error appears on index 1 (the former row 2) because superRefine indices are not re-mapped

scenarios.name: Duplicate component superRefine error not cleared after fix
scenarios.description: After triggering a duplicate-component superRefine error and then changing one component to remove the duplication, the error persists until next submission
actions: Render product form with 2 BOM rows using the same componentId
Submit to trigger duplicate-component superRefine error
Change one row's componentId to a different value
Check whether the duplicate error is still displayed
scenarios.expectedResult: Error clears immediately when the duplication is resolved
scenarios.actualResult: Error persists until the form is re-submitted because superRefine only runs on submit

scenarios.name: Material item type accepts BOM rows via API
scenarios.description: The Zod schema does not restrict BOM rows to product item type, so a material can be created with BOM components via direct API call
actions: Create a payload with type 'material' and a non-empty bomComponents array
Submit via POST /api/inventory/materials
Verify response status and whether BOM rows were stored
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 rejecting BOM components on material item type
scenarios.actualResult: 201 created with BOM rows stored for a material, violating business rules

scenarios.name: Null bomMode with BOM rows bypasses all row validation
scenarios.description: Setting bomMode to null while including BOM rows causes superRefine to skip all row-level validation since it only checks quantity or percentage modes
actions: Create a product payload with bomMode set to null and non-empty bomComponents array
Submit via POST /api/inventory/products
Verify whether BOM rows were validated
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 requiring a valid bomMode when BOM rows are present
scenarios.actualResult: BOM rows pass validation unchecked because superRefine branches on bomMode value

scenarios.name: BOM row can reference a soft-deleted component
scenarios.description: A soft-deleted component still passes the FK constraint, creating a ghost BOM row referencing an item the user cannot see
actions: Create component material A
Soft-delete material A (set deletedAt)
Create a product with a BOM row referencing material A's ID
Submit via POST /api/inventory/products
Verify response status
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 rejecting the soft-deleted component reference
scenarios.actualResult: 201 created with a BOM row pointing to a soft-deleted component

scenarios.name: Concurrent BOM edits cause last-writer-wins data loss
scenarios.description: BOM updates delete all existing rows and re-insert, so two concurrent edits result in the second write completely overwriting the first with no conflict detection
actions: Create a product with BOM rows [A, B]
User 1 loads edit form, adds row C to get [A, B, C]
User 2 loads edit form, adds row D to get [A, B, D]
User 1 submits
User 2 submits
Query DB for final BOM rows
scenarios.expectedResult: Conflict detected and user notified, or merge produces [A, B, C, D]
scenarios.actualResult: Final BOM is [A, B, D] — row C from User 1 is silently lost

scenarios.name: Circular BOM dependency allowed beyond self-reference
scenarios.description: Only direct self-reference (A references A) is checked; indirect cycles like A->B->A are allowed, which can cause infinite loops in BOM resolution
actions: Create product A with BOM referencing product B
Update product B with BOM referencing product A
Verify the second update succeeds
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 rejecting the circular dependency
scenarios.actualResult: 201/200 success — circular dependency A->B->A is stored in DB

scenarios.name: Repeated mode toggles accumulate phantom values in both fields
scenarios.description: Toggling bomMode back and forth multiple times accumulates stale values in both quantity and percentage fields, with the final submit containing all accumulated phantom data
actions: Render product form with bomMode 'quantity'
Enter '10' in quantity
Switch to percentage, enter '50'
Switch back to quantity, enter '20'
Switch back to percentage, enter '75'
Submit form
Inspect submitted payload for phantom values
scenarios.expectedResult: Only the active mode's value is submitted; inactive field is always null
scenarios.actualResult: Both quantity '20' and percentage '75' are submitted, potentially with intermediate values leaking

scenarios.name: Removed row's validation errors inherited by new row at same index
scenarios.description: When a BOM row with validation errors is removed and a new row is added at the same field array index, the new row inherits the old row's error messages
actions: Render product form with 1 BOM row
Submit with invalid data to trigger errors on row 0
Remove row 0
Add a new BOM row (now at index 0)
Check whether the new row shows validation errors
scenarios.expectedResult: New row at index 0 has no validation errors
scenarios.actualResult: New row inherits the previous row's errors because errors are keyed by array index

scenarios.name: bomMode not reset when all BOM rows removed
scenarios.description: When all BOM rows are removed, bomMode retains its value (e.g., 'quantity') instead of resetting to null, which may affect future validation or form behavior
actions: Render product form with bomMode 'quantity' and 1 BOM row
Remove the BOM row
Inspect form state for bomMode value
Submit form
Verify bomMode in submitted payload
scenarios.expectedResult: bomMode is reset to null when the last BOM row is removed
scenarios.actualResult: bomMode remains 'quantity' with an empty bomComponents array

scenarios.name: Leading/trailing whitespace in name creates visual duplicates
scenarios.description: Name field does not trim whitespace, so 'Widget' and ' Widget ' are stored as different items that appear identical in the UI
actions: Create a product with name 'Widget'
Create a product with name ' Widget ' (with leading/trailing spaces)
Verify both are created successfully
Query DB to confirm both exist as separate records
scenarios.expectedResult: Name is trimmed before storage, or duplicate detected after trimming
scenarios.actualResult: Both items created as separate records; appear identical in UI lists

scenarios.name: BOM quantity silently truncates beyond column scale
scenarios.description: A BOM quantity value of '0.00001' silently rounds to '0.0000' in the numeric column, losing the meaningful part of the value without user notification
actions: Create a product with a BOM row where quantity is '0.00001'
Submit via POST /api/inventory/products
Query DB for the stored quantity value
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 validation error about exceeding decimal precision, or the exact value is preserved
scenarios.actualResult: Value silently rounded to '0.0000', effectively zero, with no user feedback

scenarios.name: Zero BOM quantity creates meaningless row
scenarios.description: '0' passes the truthiness-based presence check for quantity, creating a BOM row that means 'use zero of this component'
actions: Create a product with a BOM row where quantity is '0' and bomMode is 'quantity'
Submit via POST /api/inventory/products
Verify response status and stored value
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 rejecting zero quantity as meaningless
scenarios.actualResult: 201 created with a BOM row that has quantity 0

scenarios.name: Fabricated unit UUID passes Zod but fails at DB FK
scenarios.description: A random UUID passes Zod's string validation for unitId but causes an FK constraint violation at the DB layer, returning a generic 500
actions: Create a product payload with unitId set to a random valid UUID that doesn't exist in units table
Submit via POST /api/inventory/products
Verify response status and body
scenarios.expectedResult: 422 with a user-friendly error about invalid unit reference
scenarios.actualResult: Unhandled 500 from Postgres FK constraint violation

scenarios.name: Infinity passes Number() stock validation
scenarios.description: 'Infinity' passes the Number() based Zod refinement for stock but is not a valid Postgres numeric value
actions: Parse the item schema with stock set to 'Infinity'
Verify parse result
scenarios.expectedResult: Zod rejects 'Infinity' as not a valid number
scenarios.actualResult: Number('Infinity') returns Infinity which is truthy, passing the refinement

scenarios.name: Local units array only grows, never shrinks
scenarios.description: The localUnits state in the product form appends new units from the create-unit dialog but never removes stale entries, causing unbounded memory growth in long sessions
actions: Render product form
Create 5 new units via the inline dialog
Delete 3 of them via the units management page
Return to product form
Inspect localUnits state length
scenarios.expectedResult: localUnits reflects current state of available units
scenarios.actualResult: localUnits retains all 5 entries including the 3 deleted ones, growing indefinitely
